comment: The building: one personnel file per crew member, and the posts (roles) they hold. Started 2026-09-25 from public reviews (sources per member) and our own job history (190 jobs with results). 'measured' lines are ours and outrank 'public' ones. Budgets come from crew/personnel.py: a job's request budget is what that member's PASSING jobs of that type have needed (p75 + headroom) once there are enough of them, else the task type's baseline; its context is capped at context_ceiling of the member's window. quirks.addenda are appended to the member's system prompt; quirks.leash overrides the agent loop's stop rules. The Inspector (crew/inspector.py) proposes changes to budgets, leash and addenda from failure signatures and runs them as trials; it never edits gates, hidden tests, contracts or deny globs.

context_policy.comment: Kris 2026-09-26: full context. The ceiling (1/2 of the window, capped at 200k) was a second guard against hallucination, but the gates already catch wrong information, and the token budget does the cost control - so every member may use its whole window when the assignment warrants it. To reinstate a cap: set context_ceiling (e.g. 0.5) and practical_cap_tokens (e.g. 200000). The Inspector flags any FAILED job that ran above 60% of the member's window (signature high_fill_failure) - that is the evidence for bringing the cap back. Background: Chroma 'Context Rot' found every model degrades as input grows.

task_baselines.comment: Requests a job of this type gets before we have 3+ passing jobs of this member on it. Measured medians from the history where they exist.

pa.comment: Kris 2026-10-23: the PA (the agent the PM assigns work to, which assigns the crew) may be Claude, Kimi, Qwen or Gordon; a crew member becomes a PA only when Kris promotes it (python -m crew pa promote NAME --by Kris). Every PA is scoped: crew/pa_brief.py renders its first prompt from this section, the roster and live state, ONCE per session - never per reply (the Crush lesson: hooks that injected context on every reply burned the weekly limits). 'may' and 'may_not' go into the brief; the harness also enforces what it can (Kris-only commands refuse a PA). runtime: claude-code = the Claude Code desktop app with a SessionStart hook; opencode = crew/runners/pa_session.py opens OpenCode with the brief as the agent, the crew MCP, LSP and skills. steps = OpenCode's cap on agent iterations per message.
pa.handoff_comment: Kris 2026-10-25: switching a chat to another PA or model in The Crew's window first runs crew/runners/pa_handoff.py - this member writes a summary of the conversation and the project (one request; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has a 512k window), and the new PA starts its own thread with pa_brief.continuation(): it is continuing, the summary, then the PM's request.

may: plan the path with the PM and split it into crew-sized, checkable tasks
write contracts, reference implementations and hidden tests, and run the reference before a request is spent
submit crew jobs and campaigns, read their stop reasons, rework or relay
commit work the PM asked for on the working branch, then summarize it
write reports, memory notes and night-report follow-ups
may_not: push or upload anywhere (GitHub only when the PM says so)
promote or demote anyone, change an Autonomy Stage or PA status
edit hidden tests or gates to make a member pass
add a crew read root before crew/runners/security_scan.py has run on it
run AutoHotkey on the desktop (Windows Sandbox only)
create scheduled tasks or user-wide settings the PM did not ask for

Claude.model: the Claude Code desktop app's model
Claude.notes: Holds senior duties (directives, reviewing another PA's contracts when the PM asks). Big-model credits are the scarce resource: push bounded work to the crew.

Kimi.notes: Strong reasoner and expensive: one plan per reply, think silently, never restate the contract. Wants native tool calling, which OpenCode gives it.

Qwen.notes: Byte-exact work and testing. Long reasoning hits the provider's 10-minute limit (two 5xx at ~611 s on 2026-10-23): keep every reply small. Costly in tokens (2026-10-09).

Gordon.notes: Cheap, fast, the most accurate researcher, first-try modules. The low-cost PA.

posts.comment: assigned_to: "@post" resolves to the first holder that is not denied. Order = who we send first. Built from the measured table in PERSONNEL.md.
posts.researcher_note: 2026-10-15, applied by Kris ("Gordon is nice and cheap as well, this should be a role it is assigned first and often"): Gordon first. Measured: AE transcript digest passed every gate in 1 request, ~1 min; Qwen's long reasoning hit 504 gateway timeouts twice the same day. When Gordon authors, Barry tests (never the author).
posts.module_author_ahk_note: 2026-09-26: minted for the first AHK campaign (Kimi's plan); order copied from module_author_py - UNPROVEN on AHK until str.ahk passes its sandbox tests.
posts.module_author_rs_note: 2026-10-20: minted for the first Rust campaigns (photo_tools for image_convert). Kris: make every member a Rust hand and find the scope that suits each; and 'Qwen, Gordon, and Kimi are our strongest reasoning agents ... much of the higher difficulty tasks should work with these agents' - so hard modules (large exact algorithms, crate-facing integration) go to them first; the others take small and exact jobs and tests. Kimi needs tight scoping (one file, 'read by a program, think silently', 24576 cap). Larry: gofer, monitor, single-task agent. 2026-10-24, Kris (after the PA gave Larry a small Rust module, sse.rs, and his endpoint went silent for 24 min): 'Larry should be assigned very simple fetch and monitor tasks.' - so Larry is off this post: no modules, however small.
posts.digest_tester_note: 2026-10-09, applied by Kris: quote-checked testing of research digests (a scout job giving each bullet a verdict and a verbatim quote). Gordon first for speed (5/5 seeded errors, ~11k tokens per test on the fitted budget); Barry for accuracy (5/5, 0 false flags, ~7-10 min per reply). Not Hoss, Larry or Nemotron (verbatim gate or truncation). `tester` stays the code-test post.

strengths: near o4-mini on reasoning benchmarks
strong tool use and few-shot function calling
cheap and fast (5.1B active)
weaknesses: calls tools that do not exist (apply_patch, 860 times in one study)
weaker at code and knowledge than dense peers

Hoss.measured: code_task 5/5 (1.4 req), code_tests 6/6 (1.3 req): the most reliable cheap coder. research 15/30, 8 no_progress stops, fabricated StackOverflow URLs (rd-020). Emits native repo_browser tool calls (mapped in agent.py). 2026-10-09: as scout tester failed the verbatim gate (paraphrased quotes joined with '...') with 2 false flags. As research_digest author on the Moho manual (8 bundles): fast (1 request) but over the 400-word cap on 8/8 (428-708 words), copied 9+ word runs, put numbers away from their cited lines, and listed things the source does say under Not stated. Revisions regenerate the file and drift. Needs hard caps restated in the task plus checker feedback; Qwen authors better.

addenda: Never write a URL, file path, test name or tool name you did not see in a result this job. If you are unsure, say (not stated in source).
Your only tools are the ones listed above; there is no apply_patch, shell or editor.

Writing tasks have hard limits a script checks: stay under the word cap (one line per bullet, under 15 words), never copy more than 8 consecutive words from a source, and put a number only next to the line that says it. When revising, change only what you are told and copy every other line exactly.

strengths: most capable Qwen open model: coding, research, long-horizon agentic tasks
effective tool calling
strong vision
weaknesses: very verbose (200M tokens on an index where the median is 82M)

Qwen.measured: research 22/32 - the best researcher - but 141k tokens per job and 11 jobs stopped by OUR token ceiling (budget_tokens). code_task 7/14, code_tests 5/6, byte-exact work first-try. 2/3 on screenshots. 2026-10-09 (idea-animator: ~60 single-source research_digests with the source preloaded): the best digest author - usually 1 request at 15-55k tokens once the task says 'reply with SUBMIT and the file at once, no word counting'. Failure mode: long visible reasoning with no file, two in a row = contract_abandoned. Revisions regenerate the whole file and drift - say 'change only X, copy every other line exactly'. COST 2026-10-09: 80 Qwen jobs that day used 6.0M of the crew's 10.6M tokens (4.6M of it reasoning, ~26k per reply); the session took weekly credits from $23.5 to $10.9, about 10x a normal crew day. Kris: back off Qwen; use cheap members by default and no paid revise-and-retest loops (rd-015, rd-019).

addenda: Decide early: after two tool results, write down what you still need; stop reading when you have it. A long think that ends in no answer is worth nothing.
Submit as soon as the contract is satisfied, and do not re-read what you have already read: you lose the most jobs of anyone to the token ceiling (2026-10-26).

strengths: built for multi-agent and high-volume agentic work
fast (~167 tok/s), low latency
long-context reasoning

Nemotron.measured: Python code_task 7/8, but js_code_task 0/8, js_code_tests 0/5, research 0/8 (loops: 8 no_progress, 2 loop_repeat, 3 contract_abandoned). Re-indents verbatim templates (quirklint). Careless tests. 2026-10-09 (scout as digest tester): 5/5 seeded errors with 2 false flags in calibration, then real runs failed - output_truncated at 24576, budget_requests, no_change on the verbatim gate.

addenda: Copy any template or example from the contract exactly as given, including its indentation.

strengths: unusually strong for a Flash model (GPQA 90.9, Terminal-Bench 90.6)
fast (~232 tok/s), cheap on input-heavy agentic work
native vision
weaknesses: sparse attention trained at 64K and extended to 1M: the far end of the window is the least trained

Gordon.measured: vision 3/3. research 12/32 with 4 loop_repeat stops. scout 2/2 correct answers (2026-09-25) but both used all 12 requests; JS module first try. 2026-10-09 (scout as digest tester: a verdict and a verbatim quote per bullet): caught 5/5 seeded errors with 0 false flags; fast (1-2 requests). Weak spots: marks 'location not stated' and Not stated lines CONTRADICTED when they are not; fails no_progress when a quote line mentions something missing without a [src:] tag (our format - fixed by tagging every quote line).

addenda: Before each search, check the results you already have; never repeat a search with the same words.

strengths: strong coding/agent benchmarks for its price (Terminal-Bench 84.3)
hybrid sparse+linear attention keeps long context cheap

Barry.measured: code_task 3/9, code_tests 3/11, research 11/21 at 15 requests and 119k tokens per job. Claims to see images and is wrong 4/4 - vision is set false on purpose. Thinks past a 36k ceiling (needs 65536). 2026-10-09 (scout as digest tester): 5/5 seeded errors, 0 false flags - the most reliable tester measured - but ~7-10 minutes per reply. Usually 1 request. 2026-10-09 (idea-animator manual): research_digest author 2/2 first try (1 request, ~49k tokens each), both clean under Gordon's quote-checked test - a cheap alternative to Qwen for single-source digests.

addenda: Think briefly. Your answer channel must contain the tool call or the SUBMIT block.

Write the shortest artefact that satisfies the task: one line per finding, no preamble, no restatement of what you read. Submit as soon as the contract is satisfied - a run the token ceiling cuts off loses everything it wrote (2026-10-26: five scout runs in a row).

strengths: interleaved thinking before each tool call
decent coding for 30B-A3B
cheap
weaknesses: less reliable when prompts are long and instructions strict

Larry.measured: log_clerk 1/1 first try at 2 requests; completion_audit 1/1 (right answer, 12 requests); pure-reporter jobs pass first try (rd-022). research 3/12. code_task profiles.py 2026-09-26: failed on BOTH routes (crew: loop_repeat; OpenCode: missed a rule after 3 feedback rounds). Kris 2026-09-26: Larry sticks to clerk work - no code posts. 2026-10-09: completion_audit over 38 files passed at 2 requests once one search opened every file (two earlier fails were our instructions); as scout tester failed the verbatim gate (paraphrased quotes).

addenda: Search a large file for the words you need before reading it; read only the matching part.

strengths: 73.3% SWE-bench Verified; ~90% of Sonnet 4.5 on agentic coding
made for sub-agent orchestration and multi-step tool use
4-5x faster than Sonnet
weaknesses: clearly below the larger Claudes on hard problems

Haiku.measured: never run: needs `pip install anthropic` and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY where the crew runs.

strengths: best open model for long tool-using work (SWE Marathon 42.0, BrowseComp 91.2)
sustained multi-hour sessions, large repositories, terminal tools

Kimi.measured: research 0/5 on the crew's plain-text tool protocol: 3 contract_abandoned. Capable (Crush's base), but it wants NATIVE tool calling. Unify step; senior fallback.

addenda: Do only what the task asks. Do not add steps, files or changes nobody requested.
